items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: My uncle, Louis Arthur Dahl, yeah, they say that he was one of the best... That's when my father first started playing, you know. And I might have always told me that, I would just say that before he died he wrote some nice music.

ctx.x: We could check that easy, Bill. Yeah. You were talking about, who was that, an uncle of yours or somebody, a clarinet player?

My uncle, Louis Arthur Dahl, yeah, they say that he was one of the best, I mean, in those times, in those days, you know. That's when my father first started playing, you know. And I might have always told me that, I would just say that before he died he wrote some nice music. He wrote a beautiful waltz, beautiful waltz, beautiful pox style, but they never could find the music of music. I mean, someone took it. Got misplaced, something like that. It was beautiful.
Well, at one time, your father said that he was the only good clarinet player? In those days, yeah, in those days.
